text.en: A village wants a round pond with a well exactly at its centre. How can they find the centre from just a few points on the edge? Circle geometry gives the answer.

keepEnglishTerms: angle at centre = 2 x angle at circumference

text.en:
A circle is the set of all points in a plane at a fixed distance, the radius, from a fixed point called the centre.
A circle has reflection symmetry across any diameter and rotational symmetry about its centre through any angle.
Infinitely many circles pass through two given points, and their centres lie on the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining the two points.
Three points that are not on a straight line lie on exactly one circle, the circumcircle. Its centre, the circumcentre, is where the perpendicular bisectors meet.
Equal chords subtend equal angles at the centre, and the converse is also true.
A line from the centre to the midpoint of a chord is perpendicular to the chord, and a perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects it.
Equal chords are equally distant from the centre. Of two unequal chords, the longer one is closer to the centre.
The angle subtended by an arc at the centre is double the angle subtended at a point on the remaining part of the circle.

problem.en: A chord AB of length 16 cm is 6 cm from the centre of a circle. Find the radius.

text.en: The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord, so half the chord is 8 cm.

why.en: Right triangle: half chord, distance and radius.

prompt.en: How can you find the centre of a circle through three given points?

requiredIdeas.en: Draw perpendicular bisectors of two chords
Their meeting point is the circumcentre
Distance to any point is the radius

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking three collinear points define a circle

points.en: All points of a circle are at the same distance from the centre.
A unique circle passes through three non-collinear points.
The perpendicular from the centre bisects a chord; equal chords are equidistant from the centre.
The angle at the centre is double the angle on the remaining circle.
